claims: Toyota is recalling over 550,000 Highlander and Highlander Hybrid SUVs of 2021-2024 model years.
The recall is due to a second-row seat defect where the seat back may not lock.
The second-row seat defect increases injury risks.
The 2021-2024 Highlander/Hybrid recall occurred in March 2026.
The second-row seat back may fail to lock in 2021-2024 Highlander/Hybrid, violating safety standards.
The 2020-2023 Highlander recall occurred in October 2023.
The lower front bumper cover may detach in 2020-2023 Highlander, causing road hazards.
The 2024 Grand Highlander recall occurred in June 2024.
The airbag might not deploy correctly in 2024 Grand Highlander if the driver's window is down.
There are reports of 8-speed transmission issues, including whining noises and failure, in 2017-2019 Highlander.
Owners will be notified by mail starting in April 2026 for the 2021-2024 Highlander/Hybrid second-row seat recall.
Dealers will replace the return springs in the seat back recliner assemblies for free for the second-row seat recall.
Dealers will inspect, install retention hardware, or replace the front bumper cover for the 2020-2023 Highlander front bumper recall.
This information is based on reports from March 2026, including data from MotorBiscuit, autoevolution, Fox Business, and USA Today.
